mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer demand for dwellings, which correlates with positive equity market sentiment and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when HOUST rises, or the correlation between HOUST and SPX returns is statistically insignificant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% signals aggressive monetary tightening, which increases discount rates for equity valuation and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate a robust labor market that fuels consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of PAYEMS increasing and UNRATE decreasing does not produce positive 60-day SPX returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction is negative.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 signals an economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as investors adjust to lower growth expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 100 during late-cycle expansion, or the correlation between INDPRO and SPX returns is insignificant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL reading above 300 (index 1982-1984=100) indicates high inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 300, or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL as a predictor is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (index 2017=100) signals a contraction in manufacturing output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC for INDPRO is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in employment (PAYEMS) indicates a labor market overheating while manufacturing activity slows, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days due to stagflationary concerns.
failure_condition: The joint condition of INDPRO decreasing and PAYEMS increasing does not yield negative 60-day SPX returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate below 3.5% signals a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE < 3.5%, or the correlation between UNRATE and SPX returns is insignificant (p > 0.05).
